text_content: #danteph update (as of 5 p.m., 22 july 2025) the low pressure area east of aurora developed into tropical depression dante. dante is not seen to make landfall but will enhance the southwest monsoon or habagat through friday, july 25. no wind signals are expected to be hoisted. the enhanced habagat will bring significant rainfall over luzon and some parts of visayas. up to torrential rains may be expected over pangasinan, zambales, bataan, cavite, batangas, occidental mindoro, and metro manila. serious threats of flooding and landslides remain. dante was spotted 1,130 km east of northern luzon at 4 p.m. tuesday, with winds of 45 kph and gusts up to 55 kph. it is moving north northwestward at 20 kph. the disturbance will intensify up to tropical storm strength while moving northwestward over the philippine sea. it may exit the philippine area of responsibility late thursday or early friday. meanwhile, the low pressure area near batanes may either merge with the broader circulation of dante or cross extreme northern luzon towards the northern west philippine sea. #weatherpatrol | via ariel rojas, abs-cbn news

text_content: disaster response update | batanes relief mission wraps up with final airlift of 1,500 food packs in support of ongoing humanitarian assistance and disaster response (hadr) efforts in the province of batanes, two u.s. air force cv-22 osprey aircraft and two u.s. marine corps mv-22 osprey aircraft transported a total of 1,500 family food packs (ffps) provided by the department of social welfare and development (dswd) on august 3, 2025. the relief mission, which began on july 28, 2025, was spearheaded by the office of civil defense (ocd) and mobilized both philippine and u.s. air assets to deliver critical aid to typhoon-affected and geographically isolated communities in northern luzon. over the course of seven days, a total of 6,300 food packs were airlifted from clark air base in pampanga to basco, batanes, utilizing combined phu.s airlift capabilities. source: philippine air force #ndrrmc #bawatsegundomahalaga disaster response update | batanes relief mission wraps up with final airlift of 1,500 food packs in support of ongoing humanitarian assistance and disaster response (hadr) efforts in the province of batanes, two u.s. air force cv-22 osprey aircraft and two u.s. marine corps mv-22 osprey aircraft transported a total of 1,500 family food packs (ffps) provided by the department of social welfare and development (dswd) on august 3, 2025. the relief mission, which began on july 28, 2025, was spearheaded by the office of civil defense (ocd) and mobilized both philippine and u.s. air assets to deliver critical aid to typhoon-affected and geographically isolated communities in northern luzon. over the course of seven days, a total of 6,300 food packs were airlifted from clark air base in pampanga to basco, batanes, utilizing combined phu.s airlift capabilities. source: philippine air force #ndrrmc #bawatsegundomahalaga

taal volcano advisory 10 august 2025 2:00 pm this is a notice of increased seismic energy release from taal volcano. since 05:25 am today, 10 august 2025, stations of the taal volcano network (tvn) situated on taal volcano island (tvi) have been recording a pronounced increase in real-time seismic energy measurement, or rsam, simultaneous with continuing volcanic tremor. a total of nineteen (19) volcanic earthquakes has been recorded by the tvn since 09 august 2025. visual observations noted a moderate to voluminous plume from the taal main crater since the start of rsam increase. taal has been degassing low levels of sulfur dioxide or so2 since june 2025 with the latest emission measured on 8 august 2025, averaging 374 tonnes/day. these sharp increase in rsam and vigorous steaming from the main crater may lead to a phreatic or even a minor phreatomagmatic eruption. dost-phivolcs reminds the public that alert level 1 prevails over taal volcano, which means that it is still in abnormal condition and should not be interpreted to have ceased unrest nor ceased the threat of eruptive activity. at alert level 1, sudden steam-driven or phreatic or minor phreatomagmatic eruptions, minor ashfall and lethal accumulations or expulsions of volcanic gas can occur and threaten areas within tvi. dost-phivolcs strongly recommends that entry into tvi, taals permanent danger zone or pdz, especially the vicinities of the main crater and the daang kastila fissure, must remain strictly prohibited. local government units are advised to continuously prepare for potential recurrence of volcanic so2 increases and exposure of their communities and undertake appropriate response measures to mitigate the health impacts of these hazards. lastly, civil aviation authorities must also advise pilots to avoid flying above tvi as ash from any sudden eruption can be hazardous to aircraft. dost-phivolcs is closely monitoring taal volcanos activity and any new significant development text_content: atm: redas training reaches sorsogon province dost-phivolcs leads a training on "mainstreaming disaster risk reduction into the local development, contingency, and emergency preparedness planning process through the use of redas software" for sorsogon province. the training, held at cristinas resort and hotel, sorsogon city on july 21-25, 2025, features three modules including redas function to simulate earthquake hazards, such as ground shaking, liquefaction, landslides, and tsunami. mr. raden d. dimaano, head of the provincial disaster risk reduction and management office (pdrrmo), welcomed the participants while mr. franco eric o. ravanilla, sorsogon provincial administrator, sent his message of support to this initiative. training participants represent the pdrrmo, provincial planning and development office, and provincial agriculturist office, and municipalities of barcelona, bulan, bulusan, castilla, casiguran, donsol, gubat, irosin, juban, magallanes, pilar, prieto diaz, and sorsogon city. also, personnel from department of the interior and local government (dilg) sorsogon, philippine national police, and guest participants from hinundayan and malitbog in southern leyte and bacacay in albay joined the training. tag: sorsogon provincial information office - as part of its commitment in championing volcano, earthquake, and tsunami disaster risk reduction (drr) activities, dost-phivolcs leads a training on communicating phivolcs information materials and tools for school drr focal persons of the department of education (deped) davao occidental from august 5-7, 2025 at sun city suites, general santos city. in his message, dr. teresito c. bacolcol, director of dost-phivolcs, emphasized the vital role of drr focal persons in every school, facilitating the conduct of evacuation drills, checking safety plans, and hazard information awareness. your work may not always be seen, but it makes a big difference. we hope that this training gives you something useful to bring back. and more than anything, we hope it reminds you that what you do mattersquietly, steadily, and every single day, dr. bacolcol added. participants learned various topics related to volcanoes, earthquakes, and tsunami information from dost-phivolcs resource speakers. ms. fatima m. moncada, science research specialist (srs) ii, discussed key principles in drrm laws and frameworks; child rights convention; understanding hazards and disasters." ms. lucille rose d. sanico, senior srs, shared the overview of volcanic eruption hazards and impacts." she also imparted her insights on understanding volcano alert level scheme" and what to do before, during and after a volcanic eruption. a learning activity on precursory signs of an impending volcanic eruption assessed the takeaways of the participants on the given discussions. ms. joan c. salcedo, supervising srs, tackled the overview of earthquake hazards and impacts. lastly, ms. moncada lectured on landslide preparedness to the participants. being situated in an area vulnerable to earthquakes, this workshop is an opportunity to empower teachers and drr focal persons in davao occidental in responding to geologic hazards through science-based drr initiatives and relay these skills to their students and the dost-phivolcs, in collaboration with dost xii, office of civil defense (ocd) xii, philippine information agency (pia) xii, and department of the interior and local government (dilg) xii, held its phivolcs infopress: understanding and communicating geologic hazards information in region xii on july 29, 2025 at greenleaf hotel, general santos city. mr. abdul jalil d. malawan, supervising science research specialist (srs) of dost xii, welcomed the participants, composed of media practitioners, government information officers, and disaster risk reduction frontliners across central mindanao. resource speakers from dost-phivolcs provided comprehensive discussions on volcano, earthquake, and tsunami information. mr. jeffrey s. perez, supervising srs, led a session on beneath the surface: understanding the big one in region xii. ms. joan c. salcedo, supervising srs, discussed a topic on from crest to trough: understanding the science of tsunami. further, ms. charmaine v. villamil, senior srs, shared an insight on land and lava: living with active volcanoes. she also moderated the open forum to give the participants an opportunity to ask questions related to the topics. in the afternoon, mr. christian r. matullano, information officer ii of pia xii, talked about #magingmapanuri campaign: dismissing disinformation. ms. melissa mae t. garcia, srs of dost-phivolcs, facilitated the geotalks: review of commonly-used geologic terms. afterward, participants took part in a return demonstration workshop. mr. raylindo s. aninon, regional director of ocd xii, delivered his closing remarks. having experienced many earthquakes in the region for the past months, this event shares the mission in equipping our partners from the media in communicating the right information on department of agriculture bulletin no. 1 on combined effects of low pressure area and southwest monsoon issued at 12:00 nn, 24 august 2025 dost-pagasa situationer as of 8:00 am today, the low pressure area (lpa) located 405km east of hinatuan, surigao del sur has a high potential of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours. the lpa will bring cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over eastern visayas, central visayas, caraga, northern mindanao, and davao region. while the southwest monsoon and localized thunderstorms will bring partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms over the rest of the country. advisory to farmers and fisherfolk the department is advising farmers to observe and perform the following, as applicable: 1. regularly monitor the latest local weather information and updates; 2. harvest mature crops; 3. secure seed reserves, planting materials, and other farm inputs in safe and proper storage areas; 4. relocate farm machineries, equipment, and other farm tools to higher ground; 5. secure sufficient feeds and water for the possible relocation of animals; and 6. clear drainage in irrigation and rice paddies from obstructions to prevent flooding and promote fast drainage of water. meanwhile, fisherfolk are advised to: 1. secure fish cages, fish ponds, and fish stocks. perform early harvest if needed and mobilize post-harvest equipment and facilities; dost-phivolcs holds a seminar-workshop for 3r (risk reduction and resilience) tsunami ready philippines: tsunami ready community for cluster 1 - provinces of ilocos sur and ilocos norte on august 27-29, 2025 at fiesta garden hotel, bantay, ilocos sur. gathering various agencies in the region including the civil defense ilocos region, dilg ilocos region, and dost 1 - department of science and technology regional office no. 1 as well as the disaster risk reduction and management offices (drrmos) within coastal areas of ilocos norte and ilocos sur, the 3-day seminar-workshop aims to equip participants on disaster preparedness and response particularly on the threats of tsunami. mr. rhon arquelada, provincial drrmo head of ilocos sur representing governor jeremias c. singson of ilocos sur province, sent his opening remarks to the participants of the event. meanwhile, dr. ma. mylene m. villegas, deputy director of dost-phivolcs, delivered a message and introduction to disaster resilience and risk reduction and phivolcs disaster mitigation programs for tsunami. participants were immersed in a series of lectures and workshops from dost-phivolcs experts. ms. joan c. salcedo, supervising science research specialist (srs), led a lecture on tsunami overview and its impacts. further, ms. fatima m. moncada, srs ii, shared the information tools developed by dost-phivolcs like hazardhunterph and redas (tsusim) which come in handy in times of disasters like tsunami. lastly, ms. charmaine v. villamil, senior srs, discussed the measures of disaster preparedness such as natural signs, philippine tsunami information, safety preparedness measures, structural and non-structural mitigation measure, cbews overview, and ioc/unesco tsunami ready recognition program. she also taught the participants basic map reading. participants will continue to learn practical skills in tsunami preparedness in the coming days of the lecture-workshop for them to create action plans in their communities and become ready and resilient against tsunami. #3rcampaign #handaangmayalam #tsunamiready #onedost4u dost-phivolcs holds a seminar-workshop for 3r (risk reduction and resilience) tsunami ready philippines: tsunami ready community for cluster 1 - kanlaon volcano bulletin 29 july 2025 6:30 pm this serves as a notice for the lowering of kanlaon volcanos status from alert level 3 (magmatic unrest / high level of volcanic unrest) to alert level 2 (moderate level of volcanic unrest). following its last eruptive activity on 13 may 2025, kanlaon volcano has been exhibiting less frequent volcanic earthquake activity, decreased volcanic gas emitted by subsurface magma and ground deformation cycles. these observations are supported by the following monitoring parameters: 1. volcanic earthquakes recorded by the kanlaon volcano network (kvn) averaged 8 events/day with peak magnitudes of ml2.7 for the period 14 may 2025 to present (figure 1a). this marks a significant decrease from the medium-term average of 14 events/day with peak magnitudes of ml3.8 for the period 3 june 2024 to 13 may 2025. volcano-tectonic or vt earthquakes generated by rock fracturing within the edifice continue to dominate earthquake activity at kanlaon. these have mostly originated along a northwest to southeast transect of the edifice at depths of 0 to 15 kilometers below mean sea level (figure 2), suggesting a structurally controlled deep magmatic intrusion that is driving unrest. despite the decline in volcanic earthquake events, however, overall seismic energy release by the volcano, as shown by real-time seismic amplitude or rsam records (figure 1c), has not significantly decreased, highlighting uncertainty in the volcanos declining seismic behavior. 2. ash emission from the summit crater (figure 1b), which began in october 2024, has ceased after the last event on 5 june 2025. since then, activity at the crater has transitioned to quiet degassing of steam-dominated plumes. a total of 306 ash emission events have been recorded since 19 october 2024, while a total of five explosive eruptions have occurred between 3 june 2024 and 13 may 2025. 3. sulfur dioxide or so2 flux based on campaign spectrometry (figure 1d) has likewise declined to an average of 1,857 tonnes/day for the period 13 may 2025 to present. average so2 flux in excess of 4,400 tonnes/day persisted between the 3 june 2024 and 6 february 2025 explosive eruptions but began to decrease in march 2025. decreased degassing at kanlaon could indicate a pause in the intrusion of, or depletion of volcanic gas in, magma within the shallower levels of the edifice, or the sealing of magmatic gas pathways. 4. ground swelling or inflation of the kanlaon edifice has been unsteadily sustained at low rates since 2022 based on continuous global positioning system (gps) monitoring and indicated in the short-term as well by electronic distance measurements since 2024 (figure 3). a short-term deflation of the edifice began in the last week of june to first week of july 2025, suggesting a pause in the intrusion of magma or depressurization due to the reduction of volcanic gas in the volcanic system, consistent with so2 flux data. in view of the above observations, dost-phivolcs is lowering the alert status of kanlaon volcano from alert level 3 to alert level 2 to reflect the overall decreasing trend in the level of monitoring parameters. alert level 2 means that there is decreased unrest but should not be interpreted that unrest has ceased or that the threat of an eruption has disappeared, given that magma has already been intruded deep beneath the edifice. should an uptrend or pronounced change in monitored parameters forewarn of potential eruption, the alert level may be raised back to alert level 3. at such time, people residing within areas at high risk to pyroclastic density currents or pdcs who have returned after the step-down to alert level 2 must therefore be prepared for a quick and organized evacuation. conversely, should there be a persistent downtrend in monitored parameters after a sufficient observation period, the alert level will be further lowered to alert level 1. dost-phivolcs strongly recommends that at alert level 2, communities within the 4-km radius permanent danger zone or pdz should remain evacuated due to the lingering chances of short-lived explosive eruptions and sudden steam-driven or phreatic explosions that can generate life-threatening volcanic hazards such as pdcs, ballistic projectiles, rockfalls and lethal expulsions of volcanic gas. local government units must continue to prepare their communities within the pdc hazard zone for subsequent evacuation in case unrest re-escalates and progresses into magmatic eruption. increased vigilance against potential lahars and sediment-laden streamflows in channels draining the volcanic slopes must continually be exercised in case eruptive unrest resumes under heavy to intense rainfall. civil aviation authorities contractors for flood control projects across the philippines appeared before the senate blue ribbon committee on tuesday, august 19, 2025, for a probe into the nations flood management issues. alan quirante of qm builders, a cebu-based development firm, was among the seven contractors who attended the inquiry. four other contractors sent representatives, while seven more were absent but submitted written replies. the senate hearing followed a report from the presidential communications office (pco), released on august 11, which ranked cebu second nationwide in the number of flood control projects despite not being among the countrys top 10 flood-prone provinces. based on the national adaptation plan of the philippines 20232050, cebu recorded 414 completed and ongoing flood control projects between july 2022 and may 2025 -- second only to bulacan. nationwide, a total of 9,855 projects are in place, amounting to more than p545 billion. qm builders is currently ranked as the countrys fourth-largest contractor. the pco report stemmed from president ferdinand marcos jr.s directive during his june 28, 2025, state of the nation address. | via sunstar cebu text_content: the duterte brand of leadership ay isang makapangyarihan at mapagpalayang pamumuno na tunay na nagbago sa takbo ng kasaysayan ng pilipinas. mula sa pagiging mayor ng davao na kilala sa disiplina at tapang, dinala ni pangulong rodrigo duterte ang kanyang malasakit at political will sa buong bansa. hindi siya natakot harapin ang mga oligarko, sindikato, at mga abusadong opisyal. tinulungan niya maging ang mga politiko na kalaunay tumalikod sa kanya, kabilang na ang pamilya marcos, at sa kanyang panahon, ibinalik sa libingan ng mga bayani ang labi ni marcos sr., isang makasaysayang hakbang na tinanggihan ng mga naunang administrasyon. sa ilalim ng kanyang liderato, umusbong ang build build build program na nagpatayo ng libo-libong imprastruktura gaya ng expressways, airports tulad ng bicol international airport, daan-daang tulay, bypass roads, flood control projects, at maging ang kauna-unahang subway ng pilipinas. tumaas ang suweldo ng mga sundalo, pulis, at guro. sa gitna ng pandemya, matagumpay na nailunsad ang vaccination rollout, naipanalo ang laban sa kaguluhan, at naipamahagi ang ayuda sa milyon-milyong pilipino. nilansag niya ang mga teroristang maute at abu sayyaf sa marawi, pinamunuan ang rehabilitasyon ng lungsod, at isinulong ang localized peace talks sa mga rebeldeng komunista. sa pamamagitan ng ntf-elcac, libo-libong dating npa fighters ang sumuko at binigyan ng kabuhayan at bagong buhay, habang tuluyang nanghina ang cpp-npa-ndf sa ideolohiya at operasyon. ang giyera kontra droga, bagamat kontrobersyal sa mata ng mga banyaga, ay nagligtas ng libo-libong pamilya mula sa kasamaan ng droga, winasak ang drug laboratories, nahuli ang mga drug lord, at nasamsam ang bilyon-bilyong halaga ng ilegal na droga. nagpatupad siya ng massive anti-corruption campaign, kung saan libo ang nasuspinde, natanggal, at nasampahan ng kaso, kahit pa sila ay malalapit sa kapangyarihan. pinirmahan niya ang mga batas tulad ng universal health care law, free college tuition law, malasakit center act, at pinatupad ang 8888 complaint hotline para mas madali ang pagreklamo ng taumbayan sa tiwaling serbisyo ng gobyerno. naisabatas ang 10-year validity ng passport, 5 to 10-year drivers license, at isinulong ang digitization ng government transactions para mas mabilis at episyente ang proseso. sa larangan ng foreign policy, tumayo siya para sa soberanya ng pilipinas, hindi siya sunod-sunuran sa amerika o china. ipinaglaban niya ang karapatan ng bansa sa west philippine sea habang iningatan ang diplomasya. hindi siya nagpadaig sa international criminal court at ipinakita sa buong mundo na ang pilipinas ay isang malayang bansa. sa gitna ng lahat ng ito, napababa niya ang krimen, napaamo ang trapiko sa edsa sa pamamagitan ng bus rapid transit system, napakilos ang pnp at afp na may disiplina, at muling pinaniwala ang sambayanang pilipino na posible ang gobyernong may malasakit, aksyon, at tunay na serbisyo. ang kanyang pamumuno ay hindi tungkol sa pa-pogi, kundi sa konkretong resulta. si pangulong rodrigo duterte ay hindi lamang naging lider kundi naging alamat, isang simbolo ng tapang, katapatan, at pagmamahal sa bayan na hinding-hindi mabubura sa kasaysayan.

press statement dost-pagasa s & t media service quezon city, 26 august 2025 la nina watch looming la nina conditions dost-pagasa has been continuously monitoring the el nino southern oscillation (enso) in the tropical pacific. enso-neutral is most likely to persist until the august-september-october 2025 season. however, model forecasts suggest an increasing probability of short-lived la nina conditions as early as the september-october-november season until the october-november-december season. la nina (cool phase of enso) is characterized by unusually cooler-than-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial pacific. when conditions are favorable for the development of la nina within the next six months and the probability is 55% or more, a la nina watch is issued. historically, la nina is characterized by an above-average number of tropical cyclone occurrences towards the end of the year and above-normal rainfall conditions in most parts of the country that can trigger adverse impacts, including floods and landslides in vulnerable areas. dost-pagasa will continue to closely monitor the possibility of la nina conditions and its effect on the local climate. all concerned agencies and the public are encouraged to continue monitoring and take precautionary measures against their potential impacts. for more information, please call the climate monitoring and prediction section (climps), climatology and agrometeorology division (cad) at telephone number (02) 8284-0800 local 4920 and 4921 or through email: pagasa.climps@gmail.com. icymi: equipping communities with georiskph: two-day training in sogod, southern leyte the two-day georiskph training, held in partnership with the municipality of sogod, southern leyte, successfully brought together thirty-eight participants from the disaster risk reduction and management offices, planning and development offices, engineering office, environment and natural resources office, planning and development coordinator, philippine national police, and bureau of fire protection. throughout the sessions, participants were equipped with knowledge on the different applications offered by the georiskph initiative, including the geomapperph mobile and web application, hazardhunterph and its pro version, and geoanalyticsph and its pro version. at the end of the training, a re-entry action plan activity was conducted where representatives from various offices shared how they intend to adopt these applications in their respective workflows. mr. renan p. grullo from the bureau of fire protection expressed their interest in using geomapperph for fire safety inspections, while ms. sheryl lura from the rural health unit of sogod presented initiatives to improve health service delivery, emergency preparedness, and program planning by incorporating geospatial data and tools. these include mapping health facilities, overlaying population data on hazard layers using geomapperph, and utilizing hazardhunterph for health emergency planning. in his closing remarks, vice mayor atty. jose ramil g. golo expressed his gratitude to the participants and facilitators and his appreciation for this kind of initiative. he shared his hope that the applications would be integrated into the workflows of local government units, helping them equip themselves to build a safer icymi: in line with the installation and integration of the 94th community tsunami alerting station (ctas) in tarragona, davao oriental, dost-phivolcs, in partnership with the municipal government of tarragona and dost region xi - davao oriental, conducted an information, education, and communication (iec) campaign and workshop on tsunami evacuation on august 21, 2025 at the municipal gym, barangay central, tarragona, davao oriental. dost-provincial science and technology office director mirasol g. domingo sent her support through the community empowerment through science and technology (cest) program. mr. dennis d. awing of mdrrmo tarragona delivered the welcome remarks on behalf of mayor art benjie c. bulaong. participants from municipal offices and barangays learned the fundamentals of earthquake and tsunami generation through a presentation by mr. joymar c. bomboc, science research assistant. moreover, ms. jordana marie l. argamosa, science research analyst, delivered an overview on the earthquake and tsunami alerting module (etam) and tsunami simulation and impact module (tsusim) of the rapid earthquake damage assessment system (redas) software. engr. angelito g. lanuza, supervising science research specialist (srs), discussed the phivolcs earthquake intensity scale (peis) and the natural signs of an impending local tsunami, while mr. nico b. anilao, project technical aide vi, presented the philippine tsunami network and tsunami early warning system (tews) visualization. to fully understand the role of community participation in disaster preparedness, ms. joan c. salcedo, supervising srs, introduced the community-based early warning system (cbews), the 12 indicators for tsunami ready recognition program, and how to conduct a tsunami drill. participants were able to appreciate the importance of their contribution through a workshop on crafting their own initial tsunami evacuation maps with information needed for their tsunami evacuation plans, which will guide them on the routes to the designated safe evacuation site in the shortest time possible. tag: dost davao oriental #handaangmayalam #ligtastsunami #tews #ctas
